item.title: Expected · Mission Bay South Block 12 West: OCII Commission scheduled to consider authorizing the Block 12 West MOU with FOCIL-MB (about 265 affordable and 270 market-rate units; Resolution No. 23-2026) at its October 6, 2026 meeting. item.title: Correction · P2: P2 was shown as under construction. Construction has not started: SF Recreation and Park's Mission Creek Park South Extension page gives construction beginning late 2026 or early 2027 and no opening date yet. P2 now shows as existing, not yet redeveloped; the expected construction start stays on its timeline.

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel E3: Parcel E3 was shown as existing on the strength of Elevation Sky Park's July 2026 announcement that it would open with Pier Play San Francisco on Sept 19. The venue's own page (published Sept 25, 2026, checked Sept 29, 2026) confirms Pier Play San Francisco was held on Sept 19, 2026, but calls the site 'the future home of Elevation Sky Park' and gives no opening date, so E3 now shows as planned and the venue's tenant listing as announced. The record now cites that page instead of pre-event announcements and no longer says the venue 'opened to the public' or is 'fully permitted' (the June 2025 deck says 'will be fully permitted'). The 2017 approval milestone is tagged planned, not existing; the unlinked SFGATE rendering is no longer relied on; the map notes no longer say the block has no Assessor lot; and the Aug 11, 2026 Port Commission minutes now back the informational hearing. Placing the venue on Parcel E3 remains Pier & Point's own mapping decision. The Brookfield construction halt is dated 2022 (approximate) rather than April 2022, since neither source gives the month, and the Board of Supervisors vote on the Development Agreement shows first reading Oct 31 and final passage Nov 14, 2017.

item.title: Status · 1215 Michigan St: The map status changed from planned to existing. The San Francisco Chronicle (Sept 2026) reported that the site may become a data center, called the exact status of any proposal unclear and said no plans appeared to have been filed with the city; the site itself is an operating industrial yard. Also corrected: the wording that no application had been filed with SF Planning now follows the Chronicle's hedged wording, the quote from Supervisor Walton is limited to the words the paper actually quoted, the distance note marks the two-block figure as our own reckoning, and the Planning Commission hearing line no longer says none is scheduled. Its use is now 'industrial' rather than 'data_center', since the Chronicle describes the site as a crane-rental and heavy-hauling yard today.
